schema: members: name -> file, status (exact: byte-identical member; open), note. The same for libPW.a (ccv1 -O) and slibPW.a (sccv1 -O -DSEG).
compiler: v1 (ccv1, sccv1) with OLD_D24, OLD_D2CW (scodgen) and OLD_D25 (scparse) and the narrowed OLD_D20 and OLD_D52 of popt (host/OLDCC.md), dated 07/22/83 by Library.SC

move.o.note: No source in System III for the Z8000: written after pdp11/move.c (the x.ip forms as int pointers xi, yi; register order x, y, xi, yi, m). slibPW.a needs OLD_D2CW: the copy (int)x of the pointer in rr12 holds no name, the byte copy takes rl2.

regcmp.o.note: WEGA form: regs[6] (seg: a struct of 3) declared first, a counter n and a flag f as register variables; after NREGS arguments adx goes to &regs[5] (nonseg) or &cs4 (seg). PINT (int, seg long) for __sp_, adx, __rpop. The nonseg target &regs[5] is a quirk of the original (KNOWLEDGE.md).

regex.o.note: WEGA form: regex() copies the register arguments into regs[NREGS] (4, seg 1) and calls _zregex(addrc, addrl, regs, &args); in _zregex a register declaration stands between in and cur (frame slot order). The third argument of __cclass is cast to char at the three compares ((char)(ep[-1]==(CCL|RNGE)), (char)(ep[-1]==(CCL|PLUS))): an odd form that fits (extsb in the original). PINT for the stack pointers and the returns; seg __advance has long i behind gflg.

setsig.o.note: WEGA: "Segmentation violation" for "Memory fault"; n is int (*n)() (the seg member keeps the long).

xcreat.o.note: WEGA: xalloc and xfree for alloca.

cat.o.note: WEGA form: cat() copies the register arguments into regs[] (nonseg 5: char *regs[5]; seg 2: struct { char *r0, *r1; } as printf of slibc) and calls _cat(dest, regs, &args), which takes the registers first and then the stack.

xalloc.o.note: WEGA: printf("out of space \n"); return((int)cp); for fatal(); the second coalesce test of xfree repeats the first (nonseg, KNOWLEDGE.md); seg: Lastbrk long, ssgbrk on the segment of end through a static union, pointer arithmetic on struct fb (Lastbrk = cp + SIZINCRO).
